page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; a marginal note in the right margin beside the second paragraph; the printed page number at the head; a gathering signature at the foot. The left strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: sed de voluntate Dei, ex mādato Chri-sti prædicandâ omnibus, (citra distin-ctionem eam, quæ fuit in Veteri Testa-mento, excludens Reges infideles) & salvāte reipsâ omnes, ipsius gratiâ cre-dentes: ut exponit Prosper, etiam lib. 1. cap. 3. hoc est, & antecedente, & conse-quente; ut hodie loquuntur. Omnes e-nim per prædicationem Deus vocari mandavit; Judæos & Gentes; fideles & infideles; reges & subditos; dominos & servos; patres & liberos: promissa crediturïs [?] salute; quam & dabit singu-lis: uti dedit & dabit fidem, quoad in-tium, incrementum, & perseverantiam. Neque enim aliis, quàm crediturs [?], dat: etsi utrosque per prædicationem verbi invitat ad fidem, pœnitentiam, & salutem.

Non male ergo de hac invitatione Chrysostomus.Chrysostomus: Omnes salvati sunt ex parte Dei. Nisi ipsum secum pugnare dicamus; quando passim derogat viribus nostris post lapsum. ut Hom. 29. in Genes. Peccatum ubi intravit; libertatem per-

page.notes: The right-margin note is printed in two lines, "Chrysosto-" and "mus.", and is transcribed as one note. No reference mark is visible in the text beside it. The signature "D s" is partly obscured and is doubtful. The words "crediturïs" and "crediturs" are doubtful readings of "crediturus"; the printed spelling has been kept as far as it can be read. The page number 57 is printed with a dot after it.
